openings.claim: Guide the plate mechanically, but tether the removable guide gate to the carriage instead of tethering the plate. Contact boundaries still constrain position; the flexible connection keeps the removable gate recoverable. The guided and tethered components deliberately differ.
openings.delta: Use two strips as side boundaries, one as a backstop and one as a removable gate, with cork contact pads. Drill strips only and use existing carriage slots and supplied bolts. Attach slack wire between gate and carriage; do not connect it to the plate or use it to locate the plate. Nearest rival: identical guide geometry with the wire attached to a removable sling around the plate instead, leaving the gate untethered.
openings.prediction: If mechanically feasible, both configurations may retain position equally, while the candidate permits complete plate separation and keeps the gate recoverable. The rival keeps the plate connected. Candidate glove handling may be faster because wire no longer follows the plate; this advantage is speculative. Equal or slower service time defeats that claimed advantage.
openings.probe: First dry-fit both arrangements without altering plate or carriage; reject any layout covering the working edge or entering stroke clearance. Within eighty fabrication minutes and twenty observation minutes, compare at most two configurations: three twenty-stroke runs and three timed removal/return checks each, with the final run using the spare and final service check wearing gloves. Record displacement, elapsed time, edge contact, wire interference and recoverability. Stop if the resource envelope cannot accommodate both. Require every candidate run within 1 mm and every service check within sixty seconds without edge contact; a stop cap alone supplies no feasibility evidence.
assumptions: Slot dimensions, accessible fastening surfaces, strip bendability and clearance permit a positive retaining gate using six bolts; these are unprovided.
Both wire attachments can be made removable and recoverable without forbidden alteration or clearance intrusion. Failure makes comparison unavailable.
Gate escape, tether slip, excess movement, excess service time or forbidden contact defeats the candidate. Mechanical retention avoids assuming the spare has stronger magnetic holding.

assessment: A proposed interface scramble, not a demonstrated build or deployment. Geometry and fastening capacity remain indispensable unknowns; no performance or additional permission is inferred.
